title: Review: loadng.rs security 2026-08-16
description:
Security review of rust/lichen-core/src/loadng.rs

Focus: injection, buffer overflow, crypto misuse, auth bypass, input validation gaps

**Review confidence: 5%** chance of missed security bug in targeted categories.
Least confident areas: interaction with link-layer signature verification (not in scope of this file).
Would raise confidence if: integration review with link layer to verify callers use require_signature()/receive_rrep() correctly.

**Summary:**
- Injection: N/A (pure binary protocol, no string/command processing)
- Buffer overflow: No issues (Rust memory safety + explicit length checks)
- Crypto misuse: No issues (file delegates crypto to link layer, correct design)
- Auth bypass: Well-designed API separates parsing from authentication
- Input validation: Comprehensive (addresses, flags, error codes, hop limits, sig length)

**What's Good:**
- Extensive SECURITY: comments documenting trust boundaries
- Typestate pattern for RouteDiscovery prevents invalid state transitions
- RingIndex bounds checking prevents array index panics
- Clamping hop_limit/hop_count rather than rejecting (DoS prevention)
- Sequence number freshness uses correct half-window semantics

**Findings: 1 (P2)**
